title: Centered 180° pizza turn using repeated short peel strokes
objective: With YAM holding a full-scale 7-inch turning peel, rotate a roughly 300 mm partially baked pizza about 180° inside a representative closed-roof 16-inch oven. Use repeated short, low-lift strokes so some pizza-to-stone contact remains at all times, keep the pizza within 50 mm of its initial center throughout, release it top-side-up on the stone, and withdraw the peel. Cooking chemistry and food safety are outside scope.
skills: full-scale long-handled tool grasp and steering
thin-blade insertion beneath a minimally compliant crust rim
repeated tangential traction with stroke resets
success_conditions: Using only the current native trial, award full credit when wrapped final yaw after release is 150–210°, maximum pizza-center excursion is no more than 50 mm at every recorded physics frame, pizza-to-deck contact remains present throughout, the pizza stays top-side-up and entirely inside the oven, no crust damage or topping loss occurs, and the peel is fully withdrawn. Award partial credit for 90–149° yaw only when all other full-credit conditions hold. Award zero for less than 90° yaw, excursion over 50 mm, any loss of deck contact, direct gripper contact with the pizza, taking the pizza outside the oven to turn it, overturning, crust penetration, permanent rim folding, topping separation, collision damage, pose writes, fake grasp welds, disabled collisions, or unreleased peel contact. Stroke count, hand identity, and action order are diagnostic only.
industrial_value: Represents the in-oven turning operation used in pizza preparation while testing long-tool control and manipulation of a weakly constrained food item in a confined, roofed workspace. The distinctive ability is tool-mediated under-edge insertion followed by centered rotation while deck support is continuously preserved, rather than generic rigid-object turning or pizza launching.
dexterity: High: the peel must enter beneath a compliant rim without puncturing it, apply several small tangential strokes without lifting the pizza clear of the deck, limit cumulative translation, release cleanly, and clear the oven mouth.

asset_plan: Create an independently authored representative fixture rather than claiming an exact product replica. Preserve the documented 630 × 580 × 370 mm oven exterior, 16-inch capacity, 15 mm cordierite deck, and 170 × 800 × 20 mm, 0.4 kg turning peel. Use a provisional 300 mm pizza with a set rigid underside/core and shallow rim compliance limited to what blade entry requires. Treat mouth height, interior roof profile, usable deck depth, peel-edge thickness, pizza mass, friction, restitution, and rim stiffness as disclosed modeling assumptions requiring calibration. Gate development in this order: real-YAM handle grasp; full-scale reach and mouth/roof clearance; low repeated insertion strokes with no food pose scripting; tangential traction with continuous deck contact; trajectory-wide center and wrapped-yaw measurement; release clearance; and complete withdrawal. Use normal YAM joint and gripper commands only.
risk: The 800 mm handle may exceed practical YAM reach or collide with the oven mouth; a thin peel can tunnel through the rim; uncalibrated friction or compliance can produce implausible traction, lift, or folding; and center error can accumulate across strokes. Any failed native-physics gate blocks the full demonstration—equipment may not be scaled down and hidden pivots, pose control, collision disabling, or relaxed scoring are prohibited.
